Water plant continuous dosage adjustment principle based on raw water quality to ensure compliant treated water quality
Direct causal link between dosage and treated water quality, with minimal impact beyond threshold
Relationship between dosage and raw water quality reflects operator practical expertise
Raw water quality indicators are more important than treated water indicators due to wide variation in raw water vs stability in treated water
Direction of feature contributions: positive for EC-RW, NH3-N-RW, CODMn-RW, NTU-RW; negative for pH-RW, T-RW, WTR
EC-RW mechanism: high EC reflects lower purity/more ions, PACl cations neutralize negative colloid charges to promote aggregation
Higher WTR corresponds to lower SHAP values and decreased dosage
Conductivity marginal effect: nearly linear between 300 and 550 uS/cm, diminishing returns below 300 or above 550 uS/cm; bilayer compression vs low pH inhibition of Al(OH)3
NH3-N marginal effect: positive influence within 0-0.2 mg/L, less significant beyond; temperature accelerates hydrolysis, low NH3-N reduces interference
CODMn marginal effect: no clear correlation below 4 mg/L; above 4 mg/L competes for active sites with PACl, causing sharp SHAP increase

NTU-RW marginal effect: positive promoting effect generally; but increases below 2 NTU due to diffusion limitations of dispersed colloids needing electroneutralization; organic matter encapsulation in high CODMn/NTU waters
pH-RW marginal effect: required dosage decreases as pH-RW increases in 8.0-8.4 due to opposite charges of PACl and contaminants in weakly alkaline conditions
T-RW marginal effect: negative effect on dosing; endothermic hydrolysis but low temperature increases water viscosity hindering particle aggregation
pH-TW marginal effect: negative linear correlation clustered in 7.6-7.8; PACl hydrolysis releases H+; overdosing causes colloid restabilization and residual dissolved aluminum risks
NTU-TW marginal effect: no apparent linear correlation; plant NTU-TW maintained low and stable with minimal variation; charge neutralization vs colloidal protection from overdosing
AutoML (TPOT) & SHAP validation: overfitting prevented as evidenced by training R2 = 1.00 vs test R2 = 0.96 and repeated CV consistency; SHAP reveals nonlinear threshold responses

Local explanation for low-dose sample (May, Yangtze River): predicted 8.57 mg/L vs base 14.5 mg/L pulled down by pH-TW (7.906), T (22.34 °C), EC (290.2 uS/cm), CODMn (2.6 mg/L), pH (8.15)
Practical dosing optimization benefits: precise chemical addition, avoiding overdosing, empowering operator scientific decision-making
